en.title: Transforming Research into Reliable Code
en.desc: PaperCompiler is a framework designed to convert research papers into structured code repositories while maintaining the integrity of the methods described. It addresses the challenge of translating high-level descriptions and implicit assumptions from papers into explicit implementation specifications. By grounding the generated code in evidence from the original paper, it ensures that the logic and evaluation protocols are preserved, reducing errors and inconsistencies. The framework has shown significant improvements in code fidelity and reduced critical issues compared to existing methods.

zh.title: PaperCompiler：将论文转化为高保真代码的利器
zh.desc: PaperCompiler 是一个将研究论文转换为结构化代码库规范的框架，旨在保持方法逻辑和跨文件一致性，从而提高代码的准确性并减少关键错误。该框架解决了将论文高层次描述的研究方法转化为具体实现时的挑战，确保生成的代码库能够保留评估协议和方法逻辑。PaperCompiler 通过明确的规范编码实现相关证据，同时区分论文支持的信息和推断、外部委托及未解决的信息。最终，PaperCompiler 在 Paper2CodeBench 上的表现优于强基线，显著提高了代码的参考准确性。

papers.title: ExecRetrieval: Measuring the Functional-Correctness Gap in Code-Embedding Retrieval
papers.abstract: Abstract ExecRetrieval evaluates whether code embeddings can distinguish correct implementations from near-identical buggy variants, revealing that leading retrievers frequently rank incorrect near-clones above canonical solutions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Embedding-based code retrieval is a core component of coding agents and retrieval-augmented code generation, where retrieving correct code matters more than retrieving lexically similar code. Existing code-retrieval benchmarks do not plant controlled, execution-verified single-edit variants of each query's canonical implementation in the search pool, leaving the question of whether embeddings can functionally discriminate correct from near-clone-but-incorrect code unanswered in a retrieval setting. Resolving this requires a benchmark whose search pool itself contains the relevant counterfactuals -- execution-verified buggy variants near-identical to each canonical -- so that a retriever's rank ordering can be directly tested for functional discrimination rather than topical or identity overlap. We introduce ExecRetrieval, 939 Python tasks each paired with one execution-verified canonical implementation and up to four execution-verified buggy distractors, each generated by a mechanical mutation making a single targeted edit, and evaluate 23 dense embedding configurations plus BM25 under provider-native invocation with paired McNemar tests and query-level bootstrap intervals. With near-clone counterfactuals in the pool, the top hosted system reaches exec@10 = 1.00 but only exec@1 = 0.331; rank-1 misses are paired buggy variants 91.5-99.4% of the time across the four leading systems, and the canonical scores below at least one of its four paired distractors in 67-78% of queries on the leading systems. The full dataset, execution oracle, embedding matrices, environment snapshot, and pairwise statistical tests are released at the URL in Appendix D.

ru.title: Когда почти идентичный код скрывает критическую ошибку
ru.desc: В работе представлен новый бенчмарк ExecRetrieval для оценки способности векторных представлений кода различать корректные реализации от почти идентичных багов. Исследование показывает, что современные системы поиска кода часто ранжируют ошибочные варианты выше правильных решений, несмотря на высокую лексическую схожесть. Бенчмарк содержит 939 Python задач с канонической реализацией и проверенными на выполнение мутантами-ошибками, полученными путём целевого редактирования. Результаты демонстрируют критический разрыв между recall@10 и recall@1 для лидирующих систем, подчёркивая необходимость семантического анализа при поиске кода.

en.title: Distinguishing Code: Correct vs. Buggy with ExecRetrieval
en.desc: The paper introduces ExecRetrieval, a benchmark designed to evaluate the effectiveness of code embeddings in distinguishing correct code implementations from similar but buggy variants. It highlights that existing benchmarks do not adequately test this capability, as they lack controlled, execution-verified buggy versions of code. By including these near-clone distractors, the study assesses how well different retrieval systems can rank correct solutions over incorrect ones. The results show that while some systems perform well overall, they often misidentify buggy variants as correct, indicating a need for improved retrieval methods in code generation tasks.

zh.title: ExecRetrieval：区分正确与错误代码的基准测试
zh.desc: 本文介绍了ExecRetrieval，一个评估代码嵌入是否能够区分正确实现与近似错误变体的基准。研究发现，现有的代码检索系统常常将错误的近似克隆排在正确解决方案之前。为了验证嵌入的功能性区分能力，ExecRetrieval创建了一个包含执行验证的错误变体的搜索池，使得检索系统的排名可以直接测试。通过对939个Python任务的评估，结果显示，尽管顶级系统在前10名中表现良好，但在第一名的准确率却相对较低，表明现有系统在处理近似错误变体时存在显著挑战。

papers.title: Exploring Collaboration between a language and a non-language agent
papers.abstract: Abstract A benchmark of collaborative chess tasks shows that integrating continuous subagent representations directly into language models via learned state tokens outperforms text-based verbalization and scales effectively.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small LLMs are increasingly deployed as orchestrators that coordinate specialized subagents to solve complex tasks through natural language. However, in many important domains like game playing and robotics, the strongest available agents are not language models. Integrating non-language agents with LLMs would require verbalization: compressing their rich continuous representations into sparse textual summaries at each interaction step. To study whether verbalization constitutes a bottleneck, we introduce LLAMIA-Bench, a suite of six diverse collaborative chess tasks spanning three facets: behavioral imitation, state assessment, and natural-language explanation. Each task instantiates a well-established chess problem that neither the LLM nor the chess engine can solve alone. To solve LLM collaboration with non-language agents, we introduce latent state internalization, which projects the subagent's continuous representations directly into the LLM's token stream as learned state tokens, with dynamic re-encoding as actions advance the environment state. Comparing internalization to verbalized integration, our experiments reveal a consistent verbalization debt: the performance gap widens throughout training and persists as the LLM scales from 4B to 14B parameters. A single 14B model, LLAMIA, trained with latent state internalization, matches or exceeds task specialists and frontier models including GPT-5.1 with tool access across all benchmark tasks, and generalizes out-of-distribution where task-specific finetunes collapse
affiliations: Adobe Media and Data Science Research (MDSR)

ru.title: Прямая интеграция непрерывных представлений агентов в LLM без текстовой вербализации
ru.desc: В статье представлен бенчмарк LLAMIA-Bench для оценки совместной работы большых языковых моделей с специализированными агентами на примере задач в шахматах. Авторы вводят метод латентной интернализации состояния, который проецирует непрерывные представления агента напрямую в поток токенов LLM в виде обучаемых токенов состояния, избегая необходимости вербализации. Эксперименты показывают, что интернализация последовательно превосходит текстовый подход, и этот разрыв производительности растёт по мере масштабирования модели от 4B до 14B параметров. Модель LLAMIA, обученная с латентной интернализацией, достигает результатов сопоставимых с граничными моделями вроде GPT-5.1 и демонстрирует улучшенную обобщаемость на внедомённых данных.

en.title: Revolutionizing LLM Collaboration with Direct State Integration
en.desc: This paper presents a new approach to enhance the performance of language models (LLMs) in collaborative tasks, specifically in chess, by integrating continuous representations from specialized subagents directly into the LLM's processing. The authors introduce LLAMIA-Bench, a benchmark that evaluates how well LLMs can collaborate with non-language agents without relying on verbalization, which often compresses rich information into less informative text. They propose a method called latent state internalization, which allows the LLM to utilize the continuous state of subagents as learned tokens, improving task performance. The results show that this method significantly outperforms traditional verbalization techniques, especially as the model scales in size, demonstrating that direct integration leads to better collaboration and task-solving capabilities.

zh.title: 潜在状态内化：提升协作智能的关键
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种新的方法，称为潜在状态内化，旨在将非语言代理的连续表示直接集成到大型语言模型（LLM）中。通过这种方法，研究人员发现与传统的文本化方法相比，性能显著提升，尤其是在复杂的协作象棋任务中。实验表明，文本化会造成性能瓶颈，而潜在状态内化能够有效缩小这一差距。最终，训练的14B参数模型LLAMIA在多个基准任务中表现优异，超越了许多专门的任务模型。

papers.title: SnapBench: Benchmarking Snap-and-Ask Multimodal Retrieval for Mobile Interactions
papers.abstract: Abstract SnapBench introduces paired corruption benchmarks for mobile snap-and-ask retrieval, revealing that image noise severely degrades multimodal retrieval and proposing an adaptive fusion method to calibrate modality reliability.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Mobile AI acts as a visual oracle, empowering users to snap a picture of something and ask for information. Snap-and-ask retrieval is now one of the most common entry points for mobile AI, yet photos are often blurry, while text questions may be short or mistyped. Existing benchmarks only test on clean inputs or do not isolate paired robustness in snap-and-ask retrieval. Therefore, we introduce SnapBench, the first paired benchmark for robust snap-and-ask multimodal retrieval, spanning 1,145 queries, 9,085 gallery items under 53 controlled corruption conditions with human annotations. We evaluate 16 multimodal retrievers, covering dual-tower encoders and embedding-based VLMs. Results show that image corruptions substantially degrade retrieval, while text corruptions mainly affect text-only retrieval and have limited impact on joint retrieval. Clean image-only retrieval often outperforms joint retrieval, indicating the coarse-text drag and the lack of cross-modal fallback under noisy inputs. SnapBench provides a controlled testbed for evaluating robust retrieval in snap-and-ask scenarios. We further propose MOOR (Modality-anchored, Outlier-aware, Optimal Reweighting), a simple adaptive fusion approach, highlighting the need for reliability-aware modality calibration in snap-and-ask retrieval.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

ru.title: Адаптивное взвешивание модальностей для устойчивого мультимодального поиска в мобильных приложениях
ru.desc: В статье представлена SnapBench — первый парный бенчмарк для оценки мультимодального поиска в сценариях мобильного snap-and-ask (фотография + вопрос) при различных типах шума. Исследователи оценили 16 моделей multimodal retrieval на 1,145 запросах и 9,085 элементах галереи под 53 различными условиями корруптации данных с разметкой человека. Результаты показали, что шумы в изображениях существенно снижают качество поиска, тогда как шумы в тексте влияют слабо, и чистые изображения часто работают лучше совместного использования модальностей. Авторы предложили MOOR — адаптивный метод слияния модальностей с калибровкой надежности каждого модального потока для устойчивого поиска при наличии шума.

en.title: Enhancing Mobile AI Retrieval with SnapBench
en.desc: The paper introduces SnapBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of multimodal retrieval systems in mobile snap-and-ask scenarios. It highlights how image noise can significantly impair the performance of these systems, while text errors have a lesser impact on joint retrieval. The study evaluates various multimodal retrievers and finds that clean image retrieval often surpasses joint retrieval due to the challenges posed by noisy inputs. To address these issues, the authors propose an adaptive fusion method called MOOR, which aims to improve modality reliability in retrieval tasks.

zh.title: SnapBench：提升快照问答检索的鲁棒性
zh.desc: SnapBench 是一个针对移动快照问答检索的配对腐蚀基准，揭示了图像噪声对多模态检索的严重影响。该研究提出了一种自适应融合方法，以校准模态的可靠性。通过评估 16 种多模态检索器，结果显示图像腐蚀显著降低了检索效果，而文本腐蚀主要影响文本检索。SnapBench 为评估快照问答场景中的鲁棒检索提供了一个受控的测试平台。

papers.title: Autoregressive Mosaics: Probing 2D Spatial Reasoning in Text-Only Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Text-only large language models vary in open-ended 2D layout ability despite reliable geometry-to-code translation, with performance shaped by output medium and internal tracking of evolving geometric state rather than fixed plans.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language models (LLMs) trained only on text and code can sometimes generate programs that draw recognizable images. However, it is unclear whether this reflects an internal representation of 2D spatial layout or simply the ability to translate spatial descriptions into code. We introduce Autoregressive Mosaics (AM-Bench), a benchmark that separates these factors: First, a translation task gives a model a fully specified geometry of a picture in words as a prompt and asks for the code that produces it. Second, a layout task requires the model to compose an image from an underspecified prompt. Across eight open-weight text-and-code-only models, all models reliably translate specified geometry into code, but their open-ended layout performance differs substantially, indicating that these differences are not explained by code-generation ability alone. An output-medium ablation further shows that the interface or medium of expression that the model uses matters: replacing procedural code with raw SVG improves layout scores across all models. Finally, probing model activations shows that a coarse layout plan is present before generation, but reflects only the layout implied by the prompt. During generation, models track the evolving geometric state instead of executing an initially fixed plan. Overall, these results show that 2D spatial performance in text-only LLMs depends on both the model and the output medium, and is not explained by code-generation ability alone.
affiliations: Institute for Visual & Analytic Computing (VAC), University of Rostock

ru.title: Пространственное мышление в языковых моделях: отслеживание состояния важнее, чем кодогенерация
ru.desc: В работе исследуется способность текстовых больших языковых моделей генерировать двумерные макеты и код для рисования изображений. Авторы предлагают AM-Bench — бенчмарк, который разделяет задачу трансляции геометрии в код от задачи свободного компоирования изображения из неполного описания. Результаты показывают, что все модели надёжно переводят заданную геометрию в код, но качество открытого компоирования макетов сильно варьируется между моделями, что указывает на важность внутреннего представления пространственных отношений. Дополнительный анализ активаций моделей выявляет, что они отслеживают эволюционирующее геометрическое состояние во время генерации, а не следуют заранее составленному плану.

en.title: Unlocking 2D Layouts: Beyond Code Generation in LLMs
en.desc: This paper investigates how text-only large language models (LLMs) perform in generating 2D layouts, distinguishing between their ability to translate geometric descriptions into code and their capacity for open-ended layout creation. The authors introduce a benchmark called Autoregressive Mosaics (AM-Bench) to evaluate these capabilities through translation and layout tasks. Results show that while all models can translate specified geometry into code, their performance in creating layouts varies significantly, indicating that code-generation ability is not the sole factor. Additionally, the choice of output medium affects performance, with raw SVG yielding better results, and models demonstrate a dynamic tracking of geometric states during generation rather than following a fixed plan.

zh.title: 大型语言模型的2D布局能力与输出媒介相关
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）在生成2D布局时的表现差异，尽管它们在几何到代码的转换上表现可靠。研究表明，模型的输出媒介和内部几何状态的跟踪对生成结果有重要影响，而不仅仅是固定的计划。通过引入自回归马赛克（AM-Bench）基准，作者区分了翻译任务和布局任务，发现模型在这两种任务中的表现差异显著。最终结果表明，文本仅的LLMs在2D空间表现上依赖于模型本身和输出媒介，而不仅仅是代码生成能力。

papers.title: Kirin: Animal Motion Generation from In-the-Wild Video
papers.abstract: Abstract Kirin reconstructs 3D animal motion from video to build a large-scale dataset and generate text- and image-conditioned motion for animating 3D meshes.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Understanding animal motion is fundamental to modeling animal behavior and biomechanics, yet progress in this area lags far behind human motion research due to the scarcity of high-quality motion data. While human motion can be captured in controlled environments, it is impractical for most animal species, resulting in small, domain-limited datasets that restrict downstream applications such as animation. To address this challenge, we introduce Kirin, a framework that reconstructs motion from video, learns motion priors at scale, and generates realistic motion that can be directly applied to animated assets. Using large collections of in-the-wild animal videos, we reconstruct 3D motion sequences and pair them with captions to create AiM3D, the first large-scale dataset offering aligned video-text-motion tuples for quadruped animals. Building on this dataset, we develop a visual-guided motion generation model that conditions on both text and image to guide the generation of realistic motion across diverse animal species. Finally, by leveraging an off-the-shelf image-to-3D model, we automatically rig and animate 3D meshes using generated motion, producing ready-to-render animated animals. Together, our dataset and framework establish a new foundation for large-scale, text and image conditioned animal motion generation and animation. Project page: https://kirin-ani.github.io/.

ru.title: От видео к движению: генерация реалистичной анимации животных через мультимодальное кондиционирование
ru.desc: Kirin — это фреймворк для реконструкции 3D-движения животных из видео с целью создания крупномасштабного датасета. Авторы разработали AiM3D, первый большой датасет с выровненными кортежами видео-текст-движение для четвероногих животных, извлекая движения из натуральных видео в дикой природе. На основе этого датасета создана модель генерации движения, которая кондиционируется одновременно на текст и изображение для синтеза реалистичных движений разнообразных видов животных. Фреймворк позволяет автоматически анимировать 3D-модели с помощью сгенерированных движений, обходя необходимость дорогостоящей съёмки в контролируемых условиях.

en.title: Revolutionizing Animal Motion Animation with Kirin
en.desc: Kirin is a framework designed to reconstruct 3D animal motion from video footage, addressing the lack of high-quality motion data for animals. It creates a large-scale dataset called AiM3D, which pairs video, text, and motion data for quadruped animals, enabling better understanding of animal behavior and biomechanics. The framework also includes a visual-guided motion generation model that uses both text and images to produce realistic animations for various animal species. By integrating an image-to-3D model, Kirin automates the rigging and animation of 3D animal meshes, facilitating the creation of ready-to-render animated assets.

zh.title: Kirin：为动物动画开辟新天地
zh.desc: Kirin是一个从视频中重建3D动物运动的框架，旨在建立一个大规模的数据集，并生成基于文本和图像的运动，以便为3D模型动画提供支持。由于高质量动物运动数据的稀缺，动物运动的研究进展远远落后于人类运动研究。Kirin通过分析大量野外动物视频，重建3D运动序列，并与文本描述配对，创建了AiM3D，这是第一个提供四足动物视频-文本-运动元组的大规模数据集。该框架还开发了一种视觉引导的运动生成模型，能够根据文本和图像生成真实的动物运动，推动了动物动画的研究和应用。

papers.title: FoldingAgent: Inferring Parametric Origami Procedures from Demonstration Videos
papers.abstract: Abstract FoldingAgent uses a vision-language model with specialized tools to convert origami videos into executable parametric folding programs via sequential reasoning and physical verification.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present FoldingAgent, an agentic framework for inferring explicit parametric folding programs directly from origami demonstration videos. Our framework leverages the reasoning power of a pre-trained Vision-Language Model (VLM) equipped with a suite of specialized tools that enable the agent to simulate geometric transitions, verify physical plausibility, retrieve and compare visual content, and evaluate its own predictions. To translate visual content into folding programs, we define a parametric space that consists of the paper's geometry and a set of parametric folding actions. Unlike models that predict static crease patterns, our agent operates sequentially and possesses the ability to re-plan its actions, effectively mitigating the compounding errors inherent in multi-step folding. Our approach takes a step toward closing the gap between human origami knowledge, which is primarily shared through unstructured visual demonstrations, and computational methods, which typically rely on structured, parametric representations such as a crease pattern or an executable parametric plan. We evaluate our approach on PurelandFold, a newly curated benchmark of diverse Pureland origami videos with ground-truth geometry and action labels. Our results demonstrate that by combining VLM reasoning with a set of specialized tools and physical simulation, we can successfully transform unstructured visual demonstrations into executable, physically plausible folding procedures.

ru.title: От видео оригами к исполняемым программам складывания
ru.desc: FoldingAgent — это агентская система, которая использует визуально-языковую модель для преобразования видео оригами в параметрические программы складывания. Система оснащена специализированными инструментами для симуляции геометрических переходов, проверки физической правдоподобности и сравнения визуального содержимого. В отличие от моделей, предсказывающих статические паттерны складок, агент работает последовательно и может перепланировать свои действия, что снижает ошибки в многошаговых процессах. Подход демонстрирует способность преобразовывать неструктурированные визуальные демонстрации в исполняемые и физически правдоподобные процедуры складывания.

en.title: Transforming Origami Videos into Executable Folding Programs
en.desc: FoldingAgent is a framework that uses a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to create folding programs from origami videos. It employs sequential reasoning and physical verification to ensure that the generated programs are executable and realistic. Unlike traditional models that only predict static crease patterns, FoldingAgent can adapt its actions in real-time, reducing errors during the folding process. This approach bridges the gap between human origami techniques and computational methods, allowing for a more intuitive translation of visual demonstrations into structured folding instructions.

zh.title: 将折纸视频转化为可执行程序的智能框架
zh.desc: FoldingAgent 是一个利用视觉-语言模型的框架，能够将折纸视频转换为可执行的参数折叠程序。它通过顺序推理和物理验证，直接从折纸演示视频中推断出明确的参数折叠程序。该框架结合了预训练的视觉-语言模型和一系列专用工具，能够模拟几何变化、验证物理可行性，并评估自身的预测。与传统模型不同，FoldingAgent 具备重新规划动作的能力，有效减少了多步骤折叠中固有的累积误差。

papers.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Debias-SparseGPT reduces pruning-induced demographic bias in compressed large language models by incorporating representational debiasing during post-training sparsification.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Model compression techniques such as pruning and quantization facilitate the efficient deployment and acceleration of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, recent studies show that weight sparsification methods, such as SparseGPT, can amplify existing biases in models, with outputs varying significantly depending on persona cues in the prompt. In this paper, we introduce Debias-SparseGPT, a post-training pruning method incorporating representational debiasing using a second-order term defined over demographically contrasting inputs. We perform empirical validation of our method over a wide range of generative LLMs. Across models and sparsity regimes (25%, 50%, and structured 2:4 sparsity), Debias-SparseGPT consistently reduces pruning-induced bias compared to SparseGPT while preserving model perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Under the most restrictive 2:4 structured sparsity pattern, which most aggressively degrades model quality, augmenting the calibration set with long-context, content-rich examples further improves both downstream performance and fairness. Overall, Debias-SparseGPT advances the bias-performance trade-off while preserving the computational efficiency of sparse models.
affiliations: Laboratoire Hubert Curien, UMR CNRS 5516, Saint-Étienne, France

ru.title: Беспристрастное сжатие: баланс между эффективностью и справедливостью LLM
ru.desc: Debias-SparseGPT - это метод сжатия больших языковых моделей, который уменьшает демографическую предвзятость, возникающую при прунинге весов. Авторы показывают, что стандартные методы спарсификации, такие как SparseGPT, усиливают существующие смещения в моделях, что приводит к различным выходам в зависимости от подсказок с персоналиями. Предложенный подход использует дополнительный регуляризационный член второго порядка, определённый на демографически контрастных входных данных, чтобы одновременно снизить предвзятость и сохранить качество модели. Экспериментальная валидация демонстрирует, что метод эффективно уменьшает смещения при различных уровнях спарсности (25%, 50% и структурированная 2:4), не теряя вычислительную эффективность.

en.title: Reducing Bias in Compressed Language Models
en.desc: Debias-SparseGPT is a method designed to reduce demographic bias in large language models (LLMs) that have been compressed through pruning. It addresses the issue that traditional weight sparsification techniques can worsen biases in model outputs based on demographic cues. By incorporating representational debiasing during the post-training phase, Debias-SparseGPT effectively mitigates these biases while maintaining the model's performance metrics like perplexity and accuracy. The method has been empirically validated across various models and sparsity levels, demonstrating a significant improvement in fairness without sacrificing computational efficiency.

zh.title: 减少偏见，提升公平性！
zh.desc: Debias-SparseGPT是一种后训练剪枝方法，旨在减少压缩大型语言模型中因剪枝引起的人口统计偏见。该方法通过在剪枝过程中引入表征去偏见，使用基于不同人口特征输入的二阶项来实现。研究表明，Debias-SparseGPT在多种生成型大型语言模型上表现出色，能够在保持模型困惑度和零样本准确率的同时，显著降低剪枝引起的偏见。总体而言，Debias-SparseGPT在提高模型公平性的同时，保持了稀疏模型的计算效率。

papers.title: Sparse Readout Prism: Explaining Logit-Lens Scores in Features Instead of Tokens
papers.abstract: Abstract Sparse Readout Prism decomposes language model readouts into sparse features to isolate readout structure from corpus-dependent lens artifacts.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small A language model's prediction of its next token develops across layers, and lens methods track this process by decoding intermediate hidden states into tokens. But a lens reading reflects both the hidden state and the readout (the unembedding matrix) used to decode it. Many lenses are fit on a corpus, and we show that two lenses differing only in their fitting corpus can report different tokens for the same hidden states. We call this dependence corpus conditionality. To examine readout structure independently of the fitting corpus, we introduce Sparse Readout Prism (SRP), which decomposes the readout using only its weights and expresses any token logit or logit difference as a sum of contributions from sparse readout features. This reveals readout features as a new unit of analysis for lens readings, exposing structure that token identities can obscure and enabling comparisons across tokens, contexts, layers, and lenses. Replacing the original readout with SRP's sparse approximation reconstructs 8.9-17.3 percentage points more of the tested logit differences than the strongest of six baselines built on geometric relations among readout rows. Ablating features shifts logit differences in proportion to their SRP contributions. Although token readings vary with the fitting corpus, the dominant readout feature remains stable. Because SRP uses no corpus in its construction, it provides a control independent of the fitting corpus for lens analyses.
affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Technology, University of Cambridge

ru.title: Разреженные признаки матрицы разворачивания как независимый анализ языковых моделей
ru.desc: Статья представляет метод Sparse Readout Prism (SRP) для анализа структуры языковых моделей, который разделяет выходные представления на разреженные признаки. Авторы показывают, что традиционные методы декодирования промежуточных скрытых состояний (линзы) зависят от корпуса, на котором они обучены, и могут давать разные предсказания для одинаковых скрытых состояний. SRP решает эту проблему, используя только веса матрицы разворачивания, без обучения на конкретном корпусе, позволяя разложить любую логит-разность на вклады отдельных разреженных признаков. Метод восстанавливает на 8,9-17,3 процентных пункта больше логит-разностей, чем базовые подходы, и остается стабильным независимо от корпуса.

en.title: Unveiling Language Model Readouts with Sparse Features
en.desc: The Sparse Readout Prism (SRP) is a method that helps to analyze language model readouts by breaking them down into sparse features. This approach allows researchers to separate the inherent structure of the readout from the biases introduced by the specific corpus used for training. By focusing on the weights of the readout, SRP enables a clearer understanding of how different features contribute to token predictions, regardless of the training data. This method improves the accuracy of token logit reconstructions and provides a stable framework for comparing different lenses and contexts in language models.

zh.title: 稀疏读出棱镜：解构语言模型的读出特征
zh.desc: 稀疏读出棱镜（SRP）将语言模型的读出分解为稀疏特征，以便将读出结构与依赖语料库的透镜伪影分离。通过分析中间隐藏状态，SRP揭示了读出特征作为透镜阅读的新分析单元，能够比较不同的标记、上下文、层次和透镜。尽管标记读取会因拟合语料库而变化，但主导的读出特征保持稳定。SRP不依赖于语料库的构建，为透镜分析提供了独立的控制。

papers.title: Ignorance or Incompetence? Constructing Knowledge-Gated, Verifiable Tasks for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract A protocol separates task instructions from private convention artefacts to explicitly test agent dependence on hidden knowledge, validated by calibration tasks showing near-zero performance without access.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Professional agent tasks often depend on conventions that are absent from public corpora, yet benchmarks rarely control whether an agent has access to those conventions. We introduce a knowledge-gated task-construction protocol that separates a task instruction from a compact artefact containing private conventions, reference tables, and utility operators. Construction-time provenance, byte-identical task instructions across the provided- and withheld-artefact conditions, leak audits, and executable witnesses make dependence on the artefact explicit and testable. Across fifteen calibration tasks, one frontier agent configuration achieves a 68.0% pass rate with the artefact and 0% without it; on one task, a plausible but incorrect artefact also yields 0% across five trials. Deterministic solvers and rule corpora provide exact ground truth for structured tasks, while named criterion-level rubrics support outputs that cannot be checked by a single executable oracle. A configuration-relative calibration screen retains seven tasks satisfying our five-trial empirical knowledge-gating screen. These experiments validate the behavior of the construction protocol; they do not establish that the retained tasks improve post-training. We publicly release part of the task suite and supporting tooling at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/Knowledge-Gated-Task-Construction.

ru.title: Отделение явного знания от скрытых конвенций в тестировании агентов
ru.desc: В статье предложен протокол для создания задач, который отделяет инструкции от скрытых артефактов, содержащих конвенции и справочные таблицы, чтобы явно тестировать зависимость агента от этих знаний. Авторы показали, что передовые модели достигают 68% точности с доступом к артефактам и 0% без них, что подтверждает правильность разделения. Протокол включает проверку утечек информации, детерминированные решатели и рубрики для оценки, позволяя точно контролировать, какое скрытое знание использует агент. Исследование демонстрирует, что существующие бенчмарки часто не контролируют доступ агентов к приватным конвенциям, скрытым в тренировочных данных.

en.title: Unlocking Agent Performance: The Role of Hidden Knowledge
en.desc: This paper presents a new protocol for constructing tasks that distinguishes between task instructions and private conventions, which are often hidden from agents. The authors demonstrate that agents can perform poorly when they lack access to these hidden conventions, as shown by calibration tasks where performance dropped to near-zero without the artefact. The proposed knowledge-gated task-construction protocol allows for explicit testing of an agent's dependence on these conventions through controlled experiments. The results indicate that while some agents can succeed with the artefact, they fail completely without it, highlighting the importance of hidden knowledge in agent performance.

zh.title: 揭示智能体对隐藏知识的依赖性
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出了一种知识门控任务构建协议，旨在测试智能体对隐藏知识的依赖性。通过将任务指令与包含私有约定的紧凑工件分离，研究人员能够明确验证智能体在没有访问这些约定时的表现。实验结果显示，在十五个校准任务中，某个智能体配置在有工件的情况下通过率为68.0%，而在没有工件的情况下则为0%。这表明，私有约定对智能体的任务执行能力有显著影响。

papers.title: Small Language Models as Judges for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Small probe-based judges can replace large generative models for rubric-based reinforcement learning rewards, improving efficiency while maintaining agreement and transferability.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Rubric-based reinforcement learning extends RL beyond tasks with exact answers or rule-based verifiers by scoring responses against instance-specific criteria. However, this makes reward computation expensive: training requires repeated rubric judging, often with proprietary APIs or local generative LLM judges with 7B parameters or more. We study whether smaller language models can serve as efficient and reliable rubric-based judges. To make this question measurable, we construct PointRubric and RaR-Science-Static, two pointwise rubric-based evaluation datasets with instance-specific criteria and itemwise satisfaction labels. We compare three ways of extracting criterion-level judgments from small models: Generative verdicts, Yes/No Logprob margins, and Probe judges. Across both datasets, the Qwen3-1.7B Probe judge achieves the strongest criterion-level agreement among these methods, outperforming Generative and Logprob judges. Used as a GRPO reward model, it trains a policy from 0.232 to 0.643 on RaR-Science rubric score, compared with 0.594 for an 8B Generative judge baseline, while the baseline requires 10.7times more reward-judge time. Task and domain transfer experiments further suggest that Probe judges preserve criterion-level reward structure across settings.

ru.title: Маленькие судьи вместо больших: эффективная оценка по рубрикам в RL
ru.desc: В работе исследуется, могут ли маленькие языковые модели эффективно заменить большие генеративные модели для оценки качества ответов по рубрикам в методе обучения с подкреплением. Авторы предложили специальный метод извлечения суждений — Probe judge — и создали два датасета с критериями оценки и пошаговыми метками качества. Экспериментально показано, что модель Qwen3-1.7B с Probe судьей достигает лучшего согласия на уровне критериев и требует в 10.7 раз меньше времени на вычисление награды, чем базовый 8B генеративный судья. Метод демонстрирует хорошую обобщаемость между задачами и областями, сохраняя структуру наград.

en.title: Efficient Rubric-Based Judging with Small Language Models
en.desc: This paper explores the use of smaller language models as judges for rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) tasks, aiming to enhance efficiency without sacrificing performance. It introduces two datasets, PointRubric and RaR-Science-Static, to evaluate the effectiveness of these smaller models in providing criterion-level judgments. The study finds that the Qwen3-1.7B Probe judge outperforms larger generative models in terms of agreement and efficiency, significantly reducing the time needed for reward computation. Additionally, the results indicate that these smaller models can maintain the necessary reward structure across different tasks and domains.

zh.title: 小型探针模型提升强化学习效率
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了小型探针模型如何替代大型生成模型，用于基于评分标准的强化学习奖励，从而提高效率并保持一致性和可转移性。研究表明，使用小型语言模型作为评分标准的评判者是可行的，并且在多个数据集上表现出色。通过构建PointRubric和RaR-Science-Static两个数据集，作者比较了不同提取标准判断的方法，发现Qwen3-1.7B探针模型在标准级别的一致性上表现最佳。最终，使用探针模型作为奖励模型，显著提高了政策的评分，同时减少了所需的评判时间。

papers.title: Portfolio Risk Bounds without Cross-Asset Return Covariances: Distributional Fields from Language-Model Representations
papers.abstract: Abstract A framework using distribution-valued firm characteristics and embedding-based representations provides computable upper bounds on portfolio variance and yields low-variance allocations without cross-asset covariance estimates.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Portfolio risk assessment ordinarily relies on reliable estimates of cross-asset return covariances, which are difficult to obtain in short, high-dimensional panels. We show that firm-level distribution-valued characteristics can instead provide one-sided certificates of portfolio risk. Under maintained links from characteristics to systematic exposures and from exposures to returns, multi-firm Wasserstein-2 dispersion yields a sharp upper bound on systematic portfolio variance and a corresponding bound for standardized returns. A weighted pairwise relaxation produces an objective that is convex under a checkable condition and requires marginal volatility scales but no cross-asset return covariances. With zero firm-specific slack, the common-map scale changes the certified variance reduction but not the normalized allocation, which depends only on observed information geometry. In a 52-firm panel from 2018-2022, an allocation constructed from Qwen3-Embedding-8B news representations lies between the 0.69th and 1.33rd in-sample variance percentiles across four prespecified capped portfolio populations; equal risk weighting lies between the 21.1st and 28.6th percentiles. The lower in-sample variance ranking relative to equal risk also appears across the reported frozen language-model representations. The framework therefore distribution-valued firm information into a coherent risk bound and an implementable allocation rule constructed without cross-asset return covariances.

ru.title: Оценка риска портфеля через характеристики компаний без кросс-ковариаций
ru.desc: В работе предложена методика оценки риска портфеля, которая использует распределяющие характеристики фирм и эмбеддинги на основе встраиваемых представлений. Авторы показывают, что вместо сложных в получении оценок ковариации между активами можно использовать расстояния Вассерштейна между распределениями характеристик компаний для вычисления верхних оценок дисперсии портфеля. Оптимизационная задача сформулирована как выпуклая программа, которая требует только маргинальные волатильности активов, но не требует кросс-корреляции доходностей. На реальных данных портфель, построенный на основе эмбеддингов новостей, показывает значительно более низкую дисперсию, чем равновзвешенный портфель.

en.title: Revolutionizing Portfolio Risk with Distribution-Valued Firm Characteristics
en.desc: This paper presents a new framework for portfolio risk assessment that uses distribution-valued characteristics of firms instead of traditional cross-asset covariance estimates. By leveraging embedding-based representations, the authors derive computable upper bounds on portfolio variance, allowing for low-variance allocations. The approach utilizes multi-firm Wasserstein-2 dispersion to establish a sharp upper bound on systematic portfolio variance, which is crucial for effective risk management. The results demonstrate that this method can yield better variance rankings compared to equal risk weighting, showcasing its practical applicability in high-dimensional financial settings.

zh.title: 利用分布值特征优化投资组合风险
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种利用分布值公司特征和嵌入式表示的框架，能够在没有跨资产协方差估计的情况下，提供可计算的投资组合方差上限，并实现低方差配置。传统的投资组合风险评估依赖于可靠的跨资产收益协方差估计，但在短期高维数据中，这些估计往往难以获得。我们展示了公司级的分布值特征可以提供投资组合风险的一侧证书，并通过多公司Wasserstein-2散布来获得系统投资组合方差的严格上限。该框架将分布值公司信息转化为一致的风险界限和可实施的配置规则，避免了对跨资产收益协方差的依赖。

papers.title: Wasserstein-Barycentric Interaction Fields for Spatial Factor Models: Evidence from Language-Model Representations
papers.abstract: Abstract A language-model embedding field reconstructed via Wasserstein barycenters predicts peer-misalignment penalties more accurately than conventional weighting schemes.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Spatial return models take the interaction matrix as given and leave feedback uninterpreted. We construct a bandwidth-free field from firms' language-model article embedding distributions using target-anchored Wasserstein barycentric reconstruction. A quadratic exposure-adjustment problem maps feedback into a peer-misalignment penalty ratio. For 52 firms, the field, frozen from 2018-2022 news, yields a 2023-2026 penalty ratio of 3.46 (95% interval [2.89, 4.17]) and higher conditional quasi-likelihood than equal-weighted peer support or RBF weighting of the same distances. Joint penalty ratios for the barycentric and news co-mention fields are 2.33 and 0.86 with boundary calibrated tests which reject both exclusions.

ru.title: Барицентры Вассерштейна для точного прогнозирования рыночных несогласованностей
ru.desc: Исследование предлагает новый метод реконструкции поля встраиваний языковой модели с помощью барицентров Вассерштейна для предсказания штрафов за несогласованность с коллегами. Авторы используют распределения встраиваний статей языковой модели от компаний и применяют методику целевого якорирования для создания непараметрического поля. Квадратичная задача оптимизации преобразует обратную связь в коэффициент штрафа за несогласованность. Предложенный подход демонстрирует превосходную предсказательную способность по сравнению с классическими схемами взвешивания и показывает статистически значимые результаты при перекрёстной валидации на данных 2023-2026 годов.

en.title: Revolutionizing Peer-Misalignment Prediction with Wasserstein Barycenters
en.desc: This paper introduces a novel approach to predicting peer-misalignment penalties using a language-model embedding field reconstructed through Wasserstein barycenters. Unlike traditional weighting methods, this approach constructs a bandwidth-free field from firms' language-model article embeddings, allowing for more accurate predictions. The study demonstrates that the new model yields a significantly higher penalty ratio compared to equal-weighted peer support and radial basis function (RBF) weighting. The results indicate that the proposed method not only improves accuracy but also provides a robust framework for analyzing feedback in financial contexts.

zh.title: 通过Wasserstein重心提升同行不对齐惩罚预测精度
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种通过Wasserstein重心重构的语言模型嵌入场，能够比传统加权方案更准确地预测同行不对齐惩罚。我们利用目标锚定的Wasserstein重心重构，从公司的语言模型文章嵌入分布中构建了一个无带宽场。通过二次曝光调整问题，将反馈映射到同行不对齐惩罚比率。研究结果显示，在2018-2022年的新闻数据基础上，该模型在2023-2026年期间的惩罚比率为3.46，且具有更高的条件准似然性。
